# Contract Guard — Architecture & Implementation Plan (Java / Spring Boot revision)

Status: design only (no application code written yet). Revision R2: technology stack switched
from Python/FastAPI to **Java 17 + Spring Boot** per team decision; product decisions,
compatibility rules, consumer impact model, publishing state machine, database concepts, API
design and test scenarios are unchanged from R1. Grounded in the reconnaissance of the actual
starter kit: 12 OpenAPI 3.0.3 specs (quote-api, policy-api, claims-api × 4 versions), 4
consumer files, stdlib Python webhook receiver, and the verified local toolchain (see §1).

Adopted publishing policy (risk-based, warning-first):

1. Non-breaking → publish normally.
2. Breaking, no registered-consumer impact → warn; publish after acknowledgment.
3. Breaking **with** registered-consumer impact → warn on first attempt, **block** by default;
   explicit override requires mandatory justification, recorded in audit history.
4. Invalid specs (incl. unresolved `$ref`) → reject unconditionally.
5. Semver is never trusted for compatibility; version-policy violations are flagged separately.

---

## 1. Technology stack & justification

### 1.1 Verified local toolchain (inspected before choosing versions)

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| JVM on PATH | OpenJDK **25.0.5** LTS (Eclipse Temurin), `javac` 25.0.5 |
| Installed JDKs | `C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-17.0.18.8-hotspot`, `jdk-21.0.13.9-hotspot`, `jdk-25.0.5.8-hotspot`; legacy Oracle `jdk-1.8` |
| Maven | **3.9.11** installed — but **running on JDK 1.8.0_431** because `JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-1.8` (stale). Any modern build fails under this setting; every Maven invocation must run with `JAVA_HOME` pointed at a JDK 17+ install (mitigation in §1.3 and B-08) |
| Gradle | not installed |
| Docker | 29.6.2 (Podman absent) — still used to run the untouched webhook receiver |

### 1.2 Chosen stack and versions

| Layer | Choice (version) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Language level | **Java 17** (`maven.compiler.release=17`) | Team direction "Java 17 or compatible"; runs on every installed JDK (17/21/25). |
| Build/JDK toolchain | **Maven 3.9.11 + Eclipse Temurin 21.0.13** as build/runtime JDK | LTS, installed locally, mature under Maven; JDK 25 also fine as runtime but adds no value here; JDK 8 must never be selected (see B-08). |
| Framework | **Spring Boot 4.1.2** (classic starters) | Verified Nov 2026 landscape: Boot 3.5 lost OSS support 2026-06-30 (3.5.16 final free patch) and 4.0 loses OSS support 2026-12-31 — both are poor targets; 4.1 (June 2026, patch 4.1.2 of 2026-10-22) is OSS-supported until 2027-07-31, keeps the Java 17 baseline, and 4.2 is not GA until 2026-11-30. Classic starters remain the boring, documented path. |
| REST | **Spring Web** (`spring-boot-starter-web`) + **Bean Validation** (`spring-boot-starter-validation`) | Monolith REST API; declarative validation for e.g. the mandatory override justification. |
| OpenAPI parsing/validation | **Swagger Parser** `io.swagger.parser.v3:swagger-parser:2.1.48` | De-facto standard; parses OpenAPI 3.0.3 (2.1.x supports 3.0 and 3.1), resolves local `$ref`s, exposes typed `io.swagger.v3.oas.models.*` POJOs, and reports parse messages we augment with our own collect-all structural walk (§3 step 3). Java 11+ prerequisite — we run 21. |
| YAML | **Jackson 3 YAML** `tools.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-yaml` (version managed by the Boot 4 BOM) for consumer files and canonical-JSON emission | Boot 4 standardized on **Jackson 3** (`tools.jackson.*` namespace). Consumer files are simple nested maps → `JsonNode` traversal. Swagger Parser brings its own Jackson 2 transitively; the two coexist by design (different root packages; `jackson-annotations` stays `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation`, shared by both — details in B-10). |
| Persistence | **H2 in file mode** (`jdbc:h2:file:./data/contractguard`) via **Spring JDBC (`JdbcTemplate`)** — no ORM | Verified trade-off: H2 is pure-Java, version-managed by the Boot BOM, and gives **in-memory mode for tests** (`jdbc:h2:mem`) for free. SQLite would need a non-BOM driver pin and offers nothing extra here. `JdbcTemplate` + hand-written DDL keeps the thin-DAO design and avoids Hibernate dialect machinery entirely. |
| Testing | **JUnit 5 + Spring Boot Test** (`spring-boot-starter-test`): plain JUnit for pure modules, `MockMvc` for controllers, `TestRestTemplate` for full-stack integration | Standard; test DB is in-memory H2 so integration tests need no state cleanup. |
| Frontend | **Minimal vanilla HTML/CSS/JS** served from `src/main/resources/static` | No build chain; Spring serves it from the same jar. |
| Notifications | **Spring `RestClient`** (sync, 2 s timeouts) fire-and-forget | Talks HTTP to the untouched Python webhook receiver; no queue. Failure is logged, never blocks publishing. |
| Packaging/run | **Docker Compose** — new `docker-compose.app.yml` *override* alongside the untouched original `docker-compose.yml`; multi-stage `Dockerfile` (`maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21` build stage → `eclipse-temurin:21-jre` runtime) | Receiver stays a fixture ("do not change this file"); the override composes both services on the same default network. Fallback if image builds are slow on the day: a slim Dockerfile that copies a locally built jar. |

Deliberately excluded: microservices, Redis/queues, **Spring Data JPA/Hibernate**, **springdoc
openapi** (the Boot-4-compatible v3 line is an optional cut-first nice-to-have), Lombok,
MapStruct, auth systems, Testcontainers, GraalVM native, React/build tooling.

### 1.3 Environment remediation (must do at hour 0)

```powershell
# Every shell that runs Maven (or add to scripts/dev.ps1 helper):
$env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.0.13.9-hotspot"
mvn -v   # must report Java 21, not 1.8.0_431
```

Then kick off a dependency warm-up in the background immediately
(`mvn -q dependency:go-offline`) while coding pure modules — first build downloads
everything; the demo must never wait on that.

## 2. High-level architecture

Modular monolith — one Spring Boot process, strict internal layering. The core packages are
plain Java (no Spring annotations, no I/O) and independently testable; Spring lives only at
the edges.

```
                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  upload / UI ──▶│ api/  (@RestController, DTOs, @ControllerAdvice,   │
                 │        static/ frontend)                           │
                 └───┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
                 ┌────────────────┐
                 │ pipeline/      │  orchestrates the steps below (I/O boundaries)
                 └─┬────┬────┬────┘
       ┌───────────┘    │    └───────────────┐
       ▼                ▼                    ▼
 specs/          compatibility/           consumers/
 SwaggerParser   effective-schema diff    Jackson-YAML reader
 wrapper +       + rule classification    + binding normalize
 collect-all        (plain Java)          + matching by method+path-shape
 structural walk                           │
 + $ref resolve                            ▼
 + canonicalize                     impact/
 + effective schemas                finding × binding → affected consumers
 + deprecation/x-sunset scan                │
       │                                    ▼
       ▼                             policy/
 policy/           ◀── findings + impacts + semver bump        publish gate
 (plain Java)      ◀── deprecation/x-sunset scan                (5 policy rules)
       │
       ▼
 domain/ (attempt state machine) ──▶ audit/ (append-only transitions)
       │
       ▼
 notify/ (RestClient) ──HTTP POST──▶ webhook-receiver (Python kit, UNTOUCHED, :9900)
       │
       ▼
 persistence/ (JdbcTemplate + H2 file: services, spec_versions, attempts, findings,
               impacts, consumers, bindings, transitions, notifications)
```

Package responsibilities (the mandated separation):

| Package | Responsibility | Explicitly does NOT |
|---|---|---|
| `specs` | Swagger Parser wrapper (parse + typed model); **collect-all structural validation incl. every local `$ref`**; canonicalization; **effective-schema extraction** per wire location; deprecation/`x-sunset` scan | classify changes, know consumers, touch the DB |
| `compatibility` | Independent schema-level diff between two effective schema maps; classify each difference with a stable rule code + severity; cosmetic-equivalence normalization | know consumers, policy, or versions |
| `consumers` | Read consumer YAML (Jackson 3 YAML); normalize bindings (method + **path shape**); match bindings to spec operations | classify severity |
| `impact` | For each breaking finding, decide which registered consumers are affected (AFFECTED / POSSIBLE / NONE) with evidence | decide publish gating |
| `policy` | Map (breaking count, affected consumers, version bump) → required action per the 5 policy rules; **separate semver-policy findings** | perform diffs |
| `domain` | Attempt state machine; guarded transitions; audit events emitted as plain events | any I/O except through interfaces |
| `audit` | Append-only history; query API | mutate findings |
| `notify` | Structured webhook payloads to the kit receiver (`RestClient`) | retry forever / block pipeline |
| `api` | HTTP surface, DTO validation, `@ControllerAdvice` error mapping, static frontend | business logic |
| `persistence` | `JdbcTemplate` DAOs + `schema.sql` (H2 init) | business logic |

## 3. End-to-end data flow (publication pipeline)

Entry points: `POST /services/{slug}/specs` (single upload) and `POST /admin/import-kit`
(reads the untouched `specs/` + `consumers/` folders in filename order and replays step 1–10
per file). Steps:

1. **Receive**: multipart file (or raw YAML body). Capture bytes → SHA-256.
2. **Parse** (`specs`): Swagger Parser `OpenAPIV3Parser` reads content; result must expose
   `openapi: 3.0.3*`, `info.title`, `info.version`, `paths`. Non-YAML/malformed → `400`.
3. **Validate + resolve** (`specs`): combine parser messages with our own document walk —
   every `$ref` string must resolve to an existing node; **collect all** errors, not
   fail-fast (e.g. claims v1.1.0 reports `#/components/schemas/ClaimDocumnt` unresolved).
   Any error → attempt state `rejected`, HTTP `422`. **Unconditional per policy rule 4.**
4. **Duplicate/regression check**: same service + same `info.version` already stored →
   identical canonical content → idempotent no-op `200`; different content → reject `409`
   (claims file 2 vs file 3 scenario). Semver lower than current published → reject `409`.
5. **Canonicalize + extract effective schemas**: inline-expand every local `$ref` at each
   usage site (swagger-core model after parser resolution, plus our own canonical form);
   erase component names, key order, formatting; produce `effective[location]` where
   `location = (method, pathShape, scope)` and
   `scope ∈ {requestBody, param:<in>:<ordinal>, response:<status>}`. Canonical JSON is
   emitted by our own DTOs with Jackson 3 (sorted keys), not by re-serializing raw
   swagger models (containment rule B-10).
6. **Diff** (`compatibility`): compare effective maps old(current published)→new; classify
   each difference (§6 rule catalog) → `findings[]` with `breaking|warn|info`.
   First version of a service → no diff → auto-publish path.
7. **Version policy** (`policy`): semver bump type old→new computed **independently**;
   emits policy findings (`VERSION.POLICY.BREAKING_WITHOUT_MAJOR`, `MAJOR_WITHOUT_BREAKING`,
   `VERSION.UNPARSEABLE`). Never merged into compatibility findings.
8. **Deprecation scan** (`specs`→findings): newly `deprecated` fields → `DEPRECATION.ADDED`
   (+ notify readers); `x-sunset` date ≤ today while field still present → `SUNSET_PASSED`
   warn (e.g. `legacyCode` sunset `2026-11-01` already past).
9. **Impact** (`impact`): for every breaking finding → match consumer bindings (method +
   path-shape; `{id}`≡`{quoteId}`) and field paths (`premium.breakdown[].amount`) →
   AFFECTED / POSSIBLE / NONE + evidence lines.
10. **Gate** (`policy` + `domain`): persist attempt + findings + impacts in one
    `JdbcTemplate` transaction; audit transition:
    - no breaking → `auto_published` (spec stored as current version) + webhook `publish`
    - breaking, zero AFFECTED → `pending_ack` (warn + wait)
    - ≥1 AFFECTED → `blocked` (warn + wait)
    Response returns state + allowed actions + full findings.

11. **Decision** (later, human): `POST /attempts/{id}/acknowledge` (comment optional) →
    `published`; `POST /attempts/{id}/override` (**justification mandatory, enforced by
    Bean Validation**, non-blank) → `overridden_published`; `POST /attempts/{id}/abandon`.
    Every transition audited; publish/override/deprecation events POSTed to the receiver
    (webhook payload includes service, version, finding summary, affected consumers,
    justification when present).

Dry-run: `GET /diff/{slug}?from=&to=` executes steps 5–8 read-only, persists nothing.

## 4. Domain model & database schema (H2 file mode, Spring SQL init)

Same entities as R1 (database concepts unchanged): `Service`, `SpecVersion`,
`PublicationAttempt`, `Finding`, `FindingImpact`, `Consumer`, `ConsumerBinding`,
`AttemptTransition` (audit), `Notification`. DDL lives in `schema.sql`, executed by Spring
Boot SQL init (`spring.sql.init.mode=always`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), reviewed for H2
dialect: primary keys as `IDENTITY`, large JSON/YAML payloads as `CLOB`, `CHECK` constraints
supported natively.

```sql
services            (id IDENTITY PK, slug VARCHAR UNIQUE, title, owner_team, created_at TIMESTAMP)
spec_versions       (id IDENTITY PK, service_id FK->services, version VARCHAR, source_sha,
                     source_filename, raw_yaml CLOB, canonical_json CLOB, effective_json CLOB,
                     state VARCHAR CHECK(state IN ('published','superseded')),
                     published_at TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(service_id, version))
publication_attempts(id IDENTITY PK, service_id FK, incoming_version, source_sha, raw_yaml CLOB,
                     canonical_json CLOB, state VARCHAR CHECK(state IN
                       ('received','rejected','auto_published','pending_ack',
                        'blocked','published','overridden_published','abandoned','failed')),
                     breaking_count INT, required_action, created_at TIMESTAMP, decided_at TIMESTAMP,
                     decided_by, justification CLOB, note CLOB)
findings            (id IDENTITY PK, attempt_id FK, code, severity VARCHAR CHECK(severity IN
                       ('breaking','warn','info')),
                     scope, method, path, location, field_path, detail, old_json CLOB, new_json CLOB)
finding_impacts     (id IDENTITY PK, finding_id FK, consumer, level VARCHAR CHECK(level IN
                       ('affected','possible','none')), evidence_json CLOB)
consumer_definitions(id IDENTITY PK, name VARCHAR UNIQUE, team, raw_yaml CLOB, source_sha, active,
                     created_at TIMESTAMP, replaced_at TIMESTAMP)   -- re-upload replaces active row
consumer_bindings   (id IDENTITY PK, consumer_id FK, provider_slug, method, path_raw,
                     path_shape, sends_json CLOB, reads_json CLOB)
attempt_transitions (id IDENTITY PK, attempt_id FK, from_state, to_state, actor, comment,
                     created_at TIMESTAMP)                          -- append-only, never updated
notifications       (id IDENTITY PK, kind, service, version, payload_json CLOB, target_url,
                     status, created_at TIMESTAMP, delivered_at TIMESTAMP)
```

Notes (unchanged in substance):
- `spec_versions` rows are created **only** when a version actually becomes current
  (auto-publish or post-ack/override). Rejected/blocked attempts live only in
  `publication_attempts` (+audit), so rejected claims v1.1.0 never blocks the fixed v1.1.0.
- `finding_impacts` is the denormalized join that answers "who breaks if this publishes?"
- DAO = thin `JdbcTemplate` repositories in `persistence`; one transaction per pipeline
  stage (`@Transactional` at the pipeline boundary). H2 file DB is single-process: the app
  holds the lock (don't open a second process against the same file).

## 5. REST API design

Base: `http://localhost:8000` (env `PORT_APP` / `server.port`). JSON errors:
`{"error": {"code", "message", "details": [...]}}` via `@ControllerAdvice`.

| Method & path | Purpose | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /services/{slug}/specs` | Upload spec (multipart `file`, optional `override_title`). Runs pipeline. | `200` attempt (state per gate) | `400` not YAML · `409` duplicate-differs / regression · `422` invalid spec (all $ref errors listed) |
| `GET /services` | Registry overview incl. current versions | `200` | — |
| `GET /services/{slug}/specs` | Version list + states | `200` | `404` |
| `GET /services/{slug}/specs/{version}` | Stored spec + findings + audit link | `200` | `404` |
| `GET /diff/{slug}?from=V&to=V` | Dry-run diff (no state change) | `200` findings + policy + impacts | `404` |
| `GET /attempts/{id}` | State, findings, impacts, allowed actions | `200` | `404` |
| `POST /attempts/{id}/acknowledge` | Body `{comment?}`; only from `pending_ack` | `200` attempt=`published` | `400` wrong state |
| `POST /attempts/{id}/override` | Body `{justification}` **required non-blank**; only from `blocked` | `200` attempt=`overridden_published` | `400` wrong state · `422` missing justification |
| `POST /attempts/{id}/abandon` | From `pending_ack`/`blocked` | `200` `abandoned` | `400` wrong state |
| `POST /consumers` | Upload consumer YAML (replaces active) | `200` parsed bindings | `400`/`422` |
| `GET /consumers` / `GET /consumers/{name}` | List / bindings + current impact matrix | `200` | `404` |
| `GET /audit?service=&attempt=` | Audit history | `200` | — |
| `GET /notifications` | Webhook delivery log | `200` | — |
| `POST /admin/import-kit` | Import `specs/` + `consumers/` (read-only scan, filename order) | `200` per-file results | — |
| `GET /api/health` | Liveness + db + webhook config | `200` | — |

Identity: actor recorded from optional `X-Acting-User` header, default `"anonymous"`
(hackathon-level; see DECISIONS.md A-07).

## 6. Compatibility classification rules

*(Unchanged from R1 — product logic, not technology.)*

**Master principle (asymmetry):** the set of requests a server accepts may only *grow*, and
the set of responses it guarantees may only *shrink in promise* — any narrowing of the
accepted-request space or of the guaranteed-response space is breaking.

Canonicalization that makes cosmetic reorganization invisible (quote 1.0.0→1.1.0 must yield
**zero** breaking findings): inline-expand all local `$ref`s → compare shapes at wire
locations → drop component names (`Premium`→`PremiumDetails`, `BreakdownItem`→`PriceLine`,
`Vehicle`/`Rider` inlined) → drop key order → treat path-template placeholder **names** as
positions (`{id}`≡`{quoteId}`). Component renames/inline moves with identical shape → at most
an `info` note, never a finding. Cycle guard: depth cap (50) + recursive-ref marker.

### Request side (consumers send)

| Code | Condition | Severity | Impact match |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REQ.REQUIRED_ADDED` | property enters `required` (policy 2.1.0 `requestedBy`) | **breaking** | bound consumers **not** declaring `sends` of that path → AFFECTED |
| `REQ.PROPERTY_REMOVED` | property deleted from request schema | **breaking** (conservative: strict servers 400 senders) | bound consumers declaring `sends` of it |
| `REQ.ENUM_NARROWED` | enum value removed (`VEHICLE` dropped) | **breaking** | all bound consumers (files don't record sent values) → AFFECTED w/ caveat |
| `REQ.TYPE_NARROWED` | accepted type set shrinks (number→integer, string→enum, format added) | **breaking** | `sends` match |
| `REQ.CONSTRAINT_TIGHTENED` | min/max/minLength/pattern tightened (e.g. new `maximum` on existing field) | **breaking** | `sends` match |
| `REQ.DEFAULT_CHANGED` | default changed | info | — |
| `REQ.PROPERTY_ADDED` | new optional property (`ncbPercent`) | info | — |
| `REQ.REQUIRED_REMOVED` | property leaves `required` | info (constraint relaxed) | — |
| `REQ.TYPE_WIDENED` / `REQ.CONSTRAINT_LOOSENED` | accepted set grows | info | — |

### Parameters

| Code | Condition | Severity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PARAM.REQUIRED_ADDED` | new required param or optional→required (quote 2.0.0 `region`) | **breaking** | path-param additions = path-shape change below; `x-internal` badge only, no auto-pass |
| `PARAM.REMOVED` | param deleted | **breaking** | — |
| `PARAM.REQUIRED_REMOVED` / `PARAM.ADDED_OPTIONAL` | — | info | — |
| `PATH_SHAPE.CHANGED` | template placeholder count/positions differ | **breaking** | affected = all bound consumers |
| `PARAM.RENAMED` | placeholder renamed, position+schema equal (`id`→`quoteId`) | info | cosmetic per canonicalization |

### Response side (consumers read)

| Code | Condition | Severity | Impact match |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESP.PROPERTY_REMOVED` | property deleted (`legacyCode`, `phone`) | **breaking** | consumers whose `reads` hit that path (exact, prefix, or `[]`) |
| `RESP.REQUIRED_REMOVED` | property leaves response `required` (claims 2.0.0 `amountApproved`) | **breaking** | `reads` match — field no longer guaranteed |
| `RESP.PROPERTY_RENAMED` | removed+added same parent, same type (heuristic; `amount`→`value`) | **breaking** | readers of old name (mobile-app) |
| `RESP.ENUM_WIDENED` | new enum value (`EXPIRED`) | **breaking** (strict readers) | bound readers of field → POSSIBLE tier (no file declares exhaustive matching) |
| `RESP.TYPE_WIDENED` / `RESP.CONSTRAINT_LOOSENED` | possible value space grows | **breaking** (strict readers) | POSSIBLE tier |
| `RESP.NULLABLE_ADDED` | `nullable` added | **breaking** (strict readers) | POSSIBLE tier |
| `RESP.RESPONSE_REMOVED` | documented status+schema deleted | **breaking** | all bound |
| `RESP.MEDIA_TYPE_REMOVED` | response no longer documents `application/json` | **breaking** | all bound |
| `RESP.RESPONSE_ADDED` | new documented status (claims 2.0.0 `202`) | info + advisory note | — |
| `RESP.PROPERTY_ADDED` | new optional (`taxes`, `assessorNotes`) | info | — |
| `RESP.REQUIRED_ADDED` | guarantee strengthened | info | — |
| `RESP.TYPE_NARROWED` / `RESP.CONSTRAINT_TIGHTENED` / `RESP.ENUM_NARROWED` | guarantee strengthened | info | — |

### Structure / lifecycle

| Code | Condition | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `OPERATION.REMOVED` / `PATH.REMOVED` | endpoint deleted | **breaking** (bound consumers AFFECTED) |
| `OPERATION.ADDED` | new endpoint | info |
| `REQUEST_BODY.MADE_REQUIRED` | body required added to existing op | **breaking** |
| `COMPONENT.MOVED_OR_RENAMED_SHAPE_EQUIVALENT` | reorg, zero wire diffs | info (trap detector) |
| `DEPRECATION.ADDED` | `deprecated: true` appears (policy 1.1.0) | warn (non-gating) + notify readers |
| `SUNSET_PASSED` | `x-sunset` ≤ today while field still present (`legacyCode` 2026-11-01) | warn (non-gating) |
| `SUNSET_SCHEDULED` | future `x-sunset` (phone 2027-06-30) | info |

### Version policy findings (separate channel — policy rule 5)

`VERSION.POLICY.BREAKING_WITHOUT_MAJOR` (policy 2.0.0→2.1.0: breaking under minor — the
planted violation) · `VERSION.POLICY.MAJOR_WITHOUT_BREAKING` (info) ·
`VERSION.UNPARSEABLE` (skip with note). Policy findings are displayed and audited but
**never gate** publication by themselves; gating is driven exclusively by compatibility
findings + impact results.

## 7. Consumer impact calculation

*(Unchanged from R1.)*

Binding normalization (`consumers`):
- Path shape: `/quotes/{id}` → segments `["quotes","{0}"]`; placeholder names ignored,
  positions kept. Spec `/quotes/{quoteId}` → identical shape. Method exact (uppercase).
- Field-path syntax unified: dots for nesting, `[]` after array property
  (`premium.breakdown[].amount`).

Matching algorithm per breaking finding `F` at location `(method, pathShape, scope, fieldPath)`:
1. Bindings where `provider_slug == F.service` **and** `method` equal **and** `path_shape`
   equal → candidate set. (No candidate → impact NONE; e.g. `region` param, `x-internal`.)
2. Scope/field mapping:
   - request findings ↔ consumer `sends`
   - response findings ↔ consumer `reads`
   - `REQ.REQUIRED_ADDED`: AFFECTED for candidates **not** declaring `sends[fieldPath]`
     (parent declaration counts as covering children).
   - removals/renames (`RESP.*`, `REQ.PROPERTY_REMOVED`): AFFECTED if consumer path equals
     fieldPath, or consumer path is a **prefix** of it (reads `premium` ⇒ affected by
     `premium.total` removal), or matches through `[]`.
   - `RESP.ENUM_WIDENED`/`TYPE_WIDENED`/`NULLABLE_ADDED`/`RESPONSE_ADDED`: POSSIBLE (advisory)
     — consumer files cannot express exhaustive matching.
   - `REQ.ENUM_NARROWED`: AFFECTED for all candidates with caveat "sent values not recorded
     in consumer file" (partner-portal sends `type`, values unknown).
3. Output per finding: `level ∈ {affected, possible, none}` + evidence list
   (consumer, binding path, matched read/send paths).

Gate mapping: any finding with ≥1 **affected** → attempt `blocked` (policy rule 3);
breaking findings with only possible/none → `pending_ack` (rule 2); none breaking →
`auto_published` (rule 1). Expected kit outcomes (from recon): quote 2.0.0 rename →
mobile-app affected → **blocked**; policy 2.0.0 `legacyCode` → payments-svc **blocked**,
`phone` → nobody; policy 2.1.0 → partner-portal **blocked** + version-policy violation;
claims 2.0.0 `amountApproved` → mobile-app **blocked**; quote 1.0.0→1.1.0 → auto-publish.

## 8. Publishing state machine & override workflow

*(Unchanged from R1.)*

```
 received ──invalid spec────────────▶ rejected (terminal, audited)      [rule 4]
 received ──duplicate differs/regres▶ rejected (terminal, audited)
 received ──no breaking findings───▶ auto_published ─▶ spec_versions row [rule 1]
 received ──breaking, none affected▶ pending_ack                        [rule 2]
 received ──breaking, ≥1 affected──▶ blocked                             [rule 3]

 pending_ack ──acknowledge{comment?}──────▶ published
 pending_ack ──abandon────────────────────▶ abandoned
 blocked     ──override{justification!}───▶ overridden_published
 blocked     ──abandon────────────────────▶ abandoned
```

- Guards: `acknowledge` valid only from `pending_ack`; `override` only from `blocked` and
  only with non-blank `justification` (Bean Validation `@NotBlank` + HTTP 422 otherwise);
  every transition writes `attempt_transitions` (actor, timestamp, comment/justification)
  before any state change.
- `overridden_published` stores: full findings snapshot, affected-consumer list, justification,
  actor → audit page shows "who broke what and why it was allowed".
- Version-policy violations never change the state machine; they decorate the attempt.
- Idempotent re-upload (same sha, same version) → `200` with existing attempt, no new audit
  noise.
- Webhooks on: `auto_published`, `published`, `overridden_published` (with justification +
  affected consumers), `blocked`, `DEPRECATION.ADDED`, `SUNSET_PASSED`. Payload:
  `{event, service, version, findings: [{code, severity, location, field_path}],
  affected_consumers, justification?, received_by}`. Target default
  `http://localhost:9900/contractguard` when running locally;
  `http://webhook-receiver:9000/contractguard` inside Compose (service name on the shared
  default network — set via `WEBHOOK_URL` env). Delivery is fire-and-forget (`RestClient`
  with 2 s timeouts, one retry); failure logged in `notifications`, never blocks publishing.

## 9. Error handling & validation strategy

- **Collect-all validation**: spec parse+validate gathers every error (all unresolved refs,
  missing `info.version`, …) before rejecting — one upload of claims v1.1.0 yields the full
  `ClaimDocumnt` diagnosis. Parser messages are merged with our own structural walk; the
  parser alone is not trusted to surface everything.
- Status-code map: `400` malformed upload / wrong-state action; `404` unknown resource;
  `409` duplicate-version-differs, version regression; `422` invalid spec (rule 4) and
  missing override justification; `500` unexpected, attempt → `failed`, transaction rolled
  back (no half-published state). All mapping centralized in one `@ControllerAdvice`.
- Bean Validation on request DTOs (`@NotBlank` justification etc.) fails at the boundary
  with 422, not deep in the state machine.
- Never persist a `spec_versions` row unless the attempt reaches a publish state — a
  rejected version must not poison later uploads of the corrected same version.
- Webhook failures are recorded, retried once, never fatal (`RestClient` timeouts caught and
  logged into `notifications`).
- Concurrency: H2 file DB + `@Transactional` per pipeline stage; duplicate simultaneous
  uploads of the same sha resolve to the same attempt (unique `(service_id, version)`).
- Character encoding: Maven build with `project.build.sourceEncoding=UTF-8` (local platform
  default is Cp1252); kit files are ASCII, but UTF-8 is enforced anyway.

## 10. Test plan (unit → integration → acceptance)

Unit (plain JUnit 5, no Spring context, pure packages):
- `specs`: Swagger Parser wrapper resolves chains; unresolved ref collected with
  JSON-pointer; cycle/depth guard; canonicalization makes `Premium≡PremiumDetails`,
  `Vehicle/Rider inline ≡ $ref`, `{id}≡{quoteId}`; `x-sunset` date parse (past/future/missing).
- `compatibility`: synthetic minimal pairs per rule code (required add/remove, property
  remove, enum add/remove, type widen/narrow, constraint tighten, param required add,
  response-required removal, operation add/remove, rename detection); kit-pair smoke: quote
  1→2 yields zero breaking + info note; quote 2→3 yields `RESP.PROPERTY_RENAMED` + `PARAM.REQUIRED_ADDED`.
- `consumers`: shape matching `{id}≡{quoteId}`; `/policies/{policyId}` ≢
  `/policies/{policyId}/endorsements`; field-path prefix & `[]` matching; Jackson-YAML
  reading of all four kit consumer files.
- `impact`: each tier with evidence; prefix rules; required-add exclusion rule.
- `policy`: decision table for all 5 rules; semver bump classifier; unparseable version.

Integration (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`/`TestRestTemplate`, **in-memory H2**):
- quote chain 1.0.0→1.1.0: auto-publish, zero findings beyond info.
- quote 1.1.0→2.0.0: `blocked`; mobile-app listed affected; override w/o justification → 422;
  override with justification → published; audit rows exist; webhook delivered (receiver
  stubbed only in fast tests; real receiver hit in acceptance).
- policy 1.0.0→1.1.0: deprecation warn; payments-svc notified (notification row).
- policy 1.1.0→2.0.0: `legacyCode` → payments-svc blocked; `phone` → no consumers.
- policy 2.0.0→2.1.0: blocked (partner-portal) **and** `VERSION.POLICY.BREAKING_WITHOUT_MAJOR`.
- claims 1.0.0→1.1.0 (file 2): 422 rejected, `ClaimDocumnt` named, no spec row.
- claims file 3 after file 2 rejected: publishes as 1.1.0; re-upload file 3 → idempotent 200.
- claims 1.1.0→2.0.0: `RESP.REQUIRED_REMOVED` → mobile-app blocked.
- consumer re-upload changing reads flips subsequent impact results.
- error mapping: unknown attempt → 404; acknowledge from wrong state → 400.

Acceptance (scripted against the running stack — PowerShell `Invoke-RestMethod` or a JUnit
acceptance test hitting `TestRestTemplate` with real ports; expected matrix from
reconnaissance): `POST /admin/import-kit` then assert per file: 12 specs → quote {auto, auto,
blocked, published-after-override…}, policy {auto, warn-only, blocked(payments),
blocked(partner)+version violation}, claims {rejected($ref), published, dup-idempotent,
blocked(mobile)}. Final state: current versions = quote 2.1.0, policy 2.1.0, claims 2.0.0;
audit timeline complete; the untouched webhook receiver's page visibly shows
publish/override/deprecation notifications; UI smoke (upload → findings → override dialog
enforces justification).

| Time | Milestone | Exit criterion |

# Contract Guard — Decision Log & Assumptions (Java / Spring Boot revision)

Each decision: context (grounded in the starter kit and the verified local toolchain), choice,
alternatives considered, consequences. Revision R2 changes only technology decisions
(B-series) and environment facts; all product decisions (A-series) are unchanged from R1.
Facts come from the reconnaissance of the actual files plus toolchain inspection and version
research on 2026-11-18; assumptions are explicitly marked and are the questions to confirm
with the product owner.

---

## A. Product & policy decisions (unchanged from R1)

**A-01 — Adopt the stated 5-rule publishing policy verbatim as the gate table.**
Context: risk-based, warning-first policy supplied by the team. Choice: the attempt state
machine implements exactly `auto_published | pending_ack | blocked | rejected` with the
override workflow for rule 3. Alternative rejected: scoring/severity-weighted gates
(over-engineered for 12 specs; undecidable thresholds). Consequence: gate outcomes are
explainable line-by-line from findings + impact tiers.

**A-02 — Semver is advisory only; version-policy findings are a separate channel.**
Context: policy kit plants a breaking change under a minor bump (policy-api 2.0.0→2.1.0:
`requestedBy` required + `VEHICLE` enum removed). Choice: compatibility engine computes
findings first; a separate module compares the semver bump and emits
`VERSION.POLICY.BREAKING_WITHOUT_MAJOR` etc. These decorate the attempt (red banner, audit)
but never gate. Consequence: rule 5 ("never trust semver alone") is honored literally; a
well-versioned breaking change still blocks (quote-api 2.0.0), a badly-versioned one is
flagged even when no consumer is affected.

**A-03 — Duplicate version: identical re-upload = idempotent no-op; differing content under
the same `info.version` = reject 409; rejected uploads don't reserve the version.**
Context: claims-api ships `1-initial`(1.0.0), `2-channel-and-notes`(1.1.0, broken ref) and
`3-channel-and-notes-fixed`(also 1.1.0, only the ref fixed). Choice: version identity is
claimed only by *stored* (published) versions. Upload of file 2 → rejected (invalid), so
file 3 publishes cleanly as 1.1.0; re-uploading file 3 → 200 no-op; a *different* spec with
an already-stored version → 409. Alternatives: revision chains (schema + UI cost, no
evaluation signal), silent overwrite (destroys audit integrity). Consequence: the
duplicate-version edge case is detected either way (409 or idempotent note) and never
poisons the registry. ⚠️ Assumption: evaluators prefer rejection over overwrite semantics.

**A-04 — Version regression rejected.** Incoming semver < current published → 409. Not in
the kit; cheap defensive rule preventing accidental downgrades. (Flagged as assumption A-11.)

**A-05 — `x-internal` is a badge, not an exemption.** Context: `DELETE
/internal/pricing-cache` (quote-api) carries `x-internal: true` in all versions and gains a
required `region` param in v2.0.0 — a real breaking change with zero registered consumers.
Choice: compatibility engine still reports `PARAM.REQUIRED_ADDED`; policy treats it under
rule 2 (warn + acknowledge) because impact is NONE; UI adds an "internal" badge.
Alternative rejected: auto-approving internal endpoints (hides the change from humans).
Consequence: uniform, explainable gating.

**A-06 — `x-sunset` is an enforceable deadline; deprecations trigger consumer warnings.**
Context: policy-api 1.1.0 adds `deprecated: true` + `x-sunset: '2026-11-01'` to
`Policy.legacyCode` (which payments-svc reads!) and `'2027-06-30'` to `Holder.phone`; 2.0.0
removes both. Choice: on `DEPRECATION.ADDED` → warn finding + webhook notice to the
registry (consumers reading the field are named from impact analysis); at any publish where
a field is still present with `x-sunset ≤ today` → `SUNSET_PASSED` warn (non-gating).
The 2026-11-01 date is already past (today 2026-11-18), which the kit deliberately allows
us to demonstrate. ⚠️ Assumption: sunset = "removed on/after this date", not "grace period
ends later".

**A-07 — Override authorization = mandatory justification, no auth system.**
Context: rule 3 requires an "explicit authorized override with mandatory justification".
Hackathon scope: any API client may override; justification is required (422 otherwise);
actor recorded from optional `X-Acting-User` header (default `anonymous`) into the audit
row. Alternative rejected: login/user registry (no time, no evaluation signal). ⚠️
Assumption: evaluators check justification enforcement + audit trail, not identity.

**A-08 — Consumer files are point-in-time snapshots; re-upload replaces the active
definition.** Context: README says consumer files describe usage "when the file was
written; the specs may have moved on since". Choice: one active definition per consumer
(`active` flag + history in `consumer_definitions`); impact always computed against the
active definition at attempt time. ⚠️ Assumption: `reads` = hard dependency (block on
removal), `sends` = declared fields (absence ⇒ affected by `REQUIRED_ADDED`); enum values
sent are not recorded ⇒ `REQ.ENUM_NARROWED` conservatively affects all bound consumers
with an explicit caveat (partner-portal + `VEHICLE`).

**A-09 — Impact tiers: AFFECTED gates, POSSIBLE warns, NONE clears.**
Context: consumers can't declare "I match exhaustively on status". Choice:
`RESP.ENUM_WIDENED`/`TYPE_WIDENED`/`NULLABLE_ADDED` produce breaking findings with POSSIBLE
impact (bound consumers listed as advisory, no block ⇒ rule 2 path). `RESPONSE_ADDED`
(claims `202`) is info + advisory note, not breaking. Consequence: quote 2.0.0 `EXPIRED`
lands in the warn-and-ack path, matching recon ("none break per files; strict consumers
unknowable").

**A-10 — Registry-first workflow, plus one-click kit import.** Choice: specs enter via
`POST /services/{slug}/specs`; `POST /admin/import-kit` scans the untouched `specs/` +
`consumers/` folders in filename order for the demo. ⚠️ Assumption: README leaves ingestion
mode open; both paths are provided so either evaluation style works.

## B. Technical decisions

**B-01 — Java 17 target / JDK 21 toolchain / Spring Boot 4.1.2.**
Context: team direction is Java + Spring Boot; verified environment has Temurin JDKs 17/21/25
installed, Maven 3.9.11, Docker 29.6.2, no Gradle/Podman. Verified ecosystem (2026-11-18):
Spring Boot 3.5 lost OSS support 2026-06-30 (3.5.16 final free patch) and Boot 4.0 loses OSS
support 2026-12-31 — building a new product on either is unjustifiable; 4.1 (patch 4.1.2,
2026-10-22) is OSS-supported to 2027-07-31 and keeps a **Java 17 baseline** (runs on 17–26).
Choice: `maven.compiler.release=17`; build and run on installed Temurin **21.0.13** (LTS,
mature under Maven); Docker runtime `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`. Alternatives rejected: Boot
3.5.x (unsupported), Boot 4.0.x (support cliff in six weeks), Boot 4.2 (GA only 2026-11-30 —
race), running on JDK 25 (works, adds nothing, and JDK 8 in `JAVA_HOME` is a trap — B-08).
Dependencies (version-managed where the Boot BOM provides it): `spring-boot-starter-web`,
`-validation`, `-jdbc`, `-test`; `io.swagger.parser.v3:swagger-parser:2.1.48` (latest 2.1.x,
OpenAPI 3.0+3.1); `tools.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-yaml`; `com.h2database:h2`.
Alternatives rejected: Gradle (not installed), Kotlin (team said Java), springdoc v2
(Boot-3-only; v3 optional, cut-first).

**B-02 — Effective-schema comparison via Swagger Parser resolution + own canonicalizer.**
Context: quote-api 1.0.0→1.1.0 renames components (`Premium`→`PremiumDetails`,
`BreakdownItem`→`PriceLine`), inlines `Vehicle`/`Rider`, renames path param `{id}`→
`{quoteId}` — all with zero wire change. Choice: parse with `OpenAPIParser`; keep our own
collect-all `$ref` walk (the parser's message list alone is not trusted to surface every
error); canonicalize by inline-expanding refs, erasing names/order, and comparing shapes at
wire locations `(method, pathShape, scope)`. Canonical JSON is emitted from our own DTOs with
Jackson 3 (sorted keys) rather than re-serializing swagger-core models — safe either way
since `jackson-annotations` is shared by Jackson 2 and 3, but own DTOs keep the canonical
form independent of the parser's object graph. Component renames with identical shape → info
note at most. Consequence: the trap yields zero breaking findings plus a "cosmetic reorg,
0 breaking" note that proves the engine worked. Cycle/depth guard (50) documented as
limitation (kit has no cycles).

**B-03 — Consumer matching = method + normalized path shape; placeholder names ignored.**
Context: consumer files say `GET /quotes/{id}` with `sends: [id]` while specs ≥1.1.0 use
`{quoteId}`. Choice: normalize templates to segment+ordinal (`{0}`); match method+shape;
field paths (`premium.breakdown[].amount`) mapped into the same coordinate system as
findings; prefix rule (reads `premium` ⇒ affected by `premium.total` removal); required-add
rule (affected iff consumer doesn't declare sending it). Consequence: notifications-svc and
mobile-app bindings keep matching after the rename; no false "no matching operation".

**B-04 — Breaking classification follows the guarantee asymmetry principle.**
Requests: accepted space may only grow (`REQUIRED_ADDED`, narrowing type/enum/constraints,
property removal ⇒ breaking). Responses: guaranteed space may only grow (`REQUIRED_REMOVED`,
property removal, possible-space growth ⇒ breaking); guarantee *strengthening*
(`REQUIRED_ADDED`, narrowing) ⇒ info. Rename detection (removed+added, same parent, same
type) reported once as `RESP.PROPERTY_RENAMED` with old+new names, matched against readers
of the old name (mobile-app + `amount`→`value`). Consequence: all nine planted edge cases
from recon fall out of ~15 rules without special-casing.

**B-05 — Modular monolith: pure-Java core packages, Spring only at the edges.**
`specs`, `compatibility`, `consumers`, `impact`, `policy`, `domain` contain **no Spring
annotations and no I/O** — plain JUnit-testable classes. `api`, `persistence`, `notify`,
`audit` own all Spring/I-O concerns. Rejected: microservices (no infra value), Spring Data
JPA/Hibernate (dialect machinery, lazy-loading traps, annotation overhead for 9 tables in
5 h), ORM-free raw `java.sql` (loses transaction/pool plumbing). Chosen middle ground:
**`JdbcTemplate` + hand-written `schema.sql`** — full SQL control, zero magic, the thin-DAO
design from R1 survives verbatim.

**B-06 — H2 (file mode) over SQLite; in-memory H2 for tests.**
Verified trade-off: H2 is pure-Java and version-managed by the Boot BOM → zero driver/dialect
risk, one dependency; SQLite would require pinning `org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc` outside the BOM
plus Windows file-locking quirks, with no countervailing benefit. Runtime:
`jdbc:h2:file:./data/contractguard`; tests: `jdbc:h2:mem` per context. DDL in `schema.sql`
executed by Spring SQL init (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), H2-dialect-reviewed
(`IDENTITY` PKs, `CLOB` payloads, native `CHECK`). Known constraint: single-process lock on
the file DB (documented; only the app opens it). Schema concepts identical to R1.

**B-07 — Mixed-Jackson containment (Boot 4 ↔ Swagger Parser).**
Context: Spring Boot 4 standardized on **Jackson 3** (`tools.jackson.*`); Swagger Parser
2.1.48 remains Jackson-2-based internally. Verified compatibility fact: Jackson 3 moved
group/package names to `tools.jackson` **except `jackson-annotations`**, which stays
`com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-annotations` (`com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation`
package) and is used by both — so Jackson 2 and 3 coexist on one classpath and Jackson 3 can
read swagger POJOs' annotations. Choice: our own JSON/YAML (canonical forms, consumer files,
webhook payloads) uses **Jackson 3** (`tools.jackson.dataformat-yaml`, Boot-managed);
Swagger Parser resolves its own Jackson 2 transitively and we never configure or share
mappers across the two worlds. Fallbacks: if the `tools.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-yaml`
artifact isn't resolved by the BOM, read consumer files with SnakeYAML (already transitive
via swagger-parser); if any Boot-4/Jackson-2 friction appears, `spring-boot-jackson2` is the
documented escape hatch. Consequence: no version surgery during the hackathon.

**B-08 — Environment remediation: `JAVA_HOME` fix + background dependency warm-up.**
Verified fact: `JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-1.8` makes Maven 3.9.11 run on JDK 8 —
every modern build fails under it. Choice: every Maven shell sets
`JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.0.13.9-hotspot` first (verified against
`mvn -v` reporting Java 21); optional `scripts/dev.ps1` helper does this + run. Build
encoding pinned to UTF-8 in the POM (platform default is Cp1252). At hour 0, run
`mvn -q dependency:go-offline` in the background so the first-build download never blocks
milestones. Consequence: the single most likely hour-0 failure mode is pre-empted.

**B-09 — Reuse the webhook receiver unmodified via a compose override file.**
Context: `app.py` and `docker-compose.yml` are evaluator fixtures ("Do not change this
file"). Choice: add `docker-compose.app.yml` (override) adding the `contractguard` service;
start with both files. Inside Compose the app reaches the receiver at
`http://webhook-receiver:9000/contractguard` (shared default network); locally at
`http://localhost:9900/contractguard` — selected by `WEBHOOK_URL` env with those defaults.
Receiver keeps in-memory state (documented limitation: restart clears notifications; our
`notifications` table is the durable log). Fire-and-forget `RestClient` delivery with one
retry; failures logged, never block publishing. Dockerfile is multi-stage
(`maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21` → `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`); fallback for slow first image
builds: slim Dockerfile copying a locally built jar.

**B-10 — Frontend = static vanilla JS page served from the Boot jar.** Pages: Publish
(upload + findings + ack/override dialog with enforced non-blank justification), Registry,
Consumers (+ impact matrix), Audit, Diff tool. No build chain; resources under
`src/main/resources/static`. Cut-first item if time runs short.

## C. Fact ledger (reconnaissance + environment — treated as ground truth)

Kit facts (unchanged from R1):
- All 12 specs are OpenAPI **3.0.3**, YAML, local `$ref`s only; versions: quote
  1.0.0/1.1.0/2.0.0/2.1.0, policy 1.0.0/1.1.0/2.0.0/2.1.0, claims 1.0.0/**1.1.0/1.1.0**/2.0.0.
- Planted breaking changes: quote 2.0.0 (`amount`→`value` response rename; required `region`
  on internal op; `EXPIRED` enum), policy 2.0.0 (`legacyCode`, `phone` removed), policy 2.1.0
  (`requestedBy` required, `VEHICLE` removed — under a **minor** bump), claims 2.0.0
  (`amountApproved` leaves response `required`; `202` added).
- Planted invalidity: claims v1.1.0 file 2 refs `#/components/schemas/ClaimDocumnt`
  (nonexistent; fixed in file 3, same version number).
- Planted cosmetic trap: quote 1.0.0→1.1.0 reorg with zero wire change.
- Planted lifecycle: `legacyCode` x-sunset **2026-11-01** (past), `phone` **2027-06-30**.
- Consumers: mobile-app reads `premium.breakdown[].amount` (rename victim) and
  `amountApproved` (required-removal victim); payments-svc reads `legacyCode`
  (removal victim); partner-portal sends `type`,`details` (required-add + enum-removal
  victim); notifications-svc reads only safe fields; nobody binds the internal op;
  `Holder.phone` has no readers.
- Consumer↔spec drift: `/quotes/{id}` vs `{quoteId}`.

Environment & ecosystem facts (added R2, verified 2026-11-18):
- Temurin JDKs **17.0.18 / 21.0.13 / 25.0.5** installed; `java`/`javac` on PATH = 25.0.5;
  Maven **3.9.11** installed but runs on **JDK 1.8** (`JAVA_HOME` stale) — builds fail until
  remediated; Docker **29.6.2**; no Gradle, no Podman.
- Spring Boot **3.5 OSS support ended 2026-06-30** (last free patch 3.5.16); **4.0 OSS ends
  2026-12-31**; **4.1** (Jun 2026, latest 4.1.2 of 2026-10-22) OSS-supported to **2027-07-31**,
  Java 17–26, Jackson 3 default; 4.2 GA planned 2026-11-30.
- Jackson 3 moved group/packages to `tools.jackson` **except `jackson-annotations`** (stays
  `com.fasterxml.jackson.core` / `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation`, shared with Jackson 2)
  — Jackson 2 and 3 coexist; Spring Boot 4 ships Jackson 3 default with a deprecated
  `spring-boot-jackson2` escape hatch.
- Swagger Parser latest 2.1.x = **2.1.48** (OpenAPI 3.0 + 3.1, Java 11+).

## D. Assumption ledger (to confirm with product owner)

| # | Assumption | Risk if wrong | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-01 | Kit file order (numeric prefix) = publication order | chain diffs wrong | import honors prefix order; manual upload unaffected |
| A-05 | `x-internal` doesn't exempt from gating | evaluator expects auto-pass | one-line policy tweak |
| A-06 | `x-sunset` semantics = removal deadline; "today" = server date | wrong warn timing | date logic isolated in one function |
| A-07 | Override authority = justification + actor header, no real auth | evaluator expects login | header is a stub for a real identity later |
| A-08 | `reads`=hard dep, `sends`=declared fields, enum values unknown ⇒ conservative | over/under-blocking | tiers + evidence make each case explicit |
| A-10 | Duplicate same-version different content should be **rejected** (not superseded) | evaluator expects revision chain | rejection is the loud, auditable behavior; policy isolated in one gate |
| A-11 | Version regression (lower semver) should be rejected | not in kit; unexpected 409 | easily disabled via config flag |
| A-12 | Evaluators may either upload via API or expect folder import | workflow mismatch | both entry points provided |
| A-13 | `RESPONSE_ADDED` (claims `202`) is info, not breaking | evaluator treats as breaking | single rule-code reclassification |
| A-14 | Notification target default `:9900` local / `webhook-receiver:9000` in Compose | receiver path preference | configurable via `WEBHOOK_URL` |
| A-15 | Overriding `JAVA_HOME` per-session (to Temurin 21) is acceptable for build/run | eval env rebuilds with its own env | Docker build path is env-independent; `release=17` keeps artifacts portable |
| A-16 | Boot 4 BOM manages `tools.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-yaml` | artifact not resolved | fallback: SnakeYAML (transitive via swagger-parser) for consumer files |
| A-17 | Network access for Maven Central + Docker Hub base images on the day | first build stalls | background `dependency:go-offline` warm-up; slim Dockerfile fallback copying a prebuilt jar |

## E. Out of scope (explicit)

Multi-tenant auth/RBAC; spec *authoring* or editor UI; runtime traffic verification
(consumer files are declarative snapshots, not observed traffic); cross-file/remote `$ref`
support (kit is local-only; depth guard documented); retry queues for webhooks; consumer
definition versioning beyond active+history; OpenAPI 2.0 parsing; Spring Data JPA/Hibernate;
springdoc/Swagger UI for our own API (optional cut-first); Testcontainers; GraalVM native
images; Kotlin.

Both documents revised (fixtures untouched — only the two planning files were written). Summary of what changed and why:

## Environment inspection findings (step 1)
- **Installed JDKs**: Temurin **17.0.18**, **21.0.13**, **25.0.5** (PATH `java` = 25.0.5) + a legacy Oracle JDK 8.
- **Blocker found**: `JAVA_HOME` points at `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-1.8` → **Maven 3.9.11 currently runs on JDK 8** and would fail any modern build. Every Maven shell must set `JAVA_HOME` to the Temurin 21 install first.
- No Gradle; Docker 29.6.2 still present for the receiver.

## Version selection (steps 2–3, verified against the Nov 2026 ecosystem)
- **Spring Boot 3.5 is out of OSS support (ended 2026-06-30)** and 4.0 loses support 2026-12-31 — so the plan now targets **Boot 4.1.2** (OSS-supported to 2027-07-31, Java 17 baseline, classic starters).
- Compile target **Java 17** (`release=17`), build/run on **Temurin 21**, Docker runtime `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`.
- **Swagger Parser 2.1.48** (latest 2.1.x, parses/validates 3.0.3, resolves local `$ref`s) replaces the hand-rolled parser for step 2–3 of the pipeline, augmented by our own collect-all `$ref` walk.
- **H2 file mode + plain `JdbcTemplate`** (chosen over SQLite and over JPA — H2 is Boot-BOM-managed with in-memory test mode for free; JPA adds dialect machinery with zero benefit).
- **Jackson 3 YAML** (`tools.jackson.dataformat`) for consumer files, with a documented wrinkle: Boot 4 is Jackson 3 while Swagger Parser is Jackson 2 internally — they coexist because `jackson-annotations` is shared by both (new decision B-10, with SnakeYAML and `spring-boot-jackson2` fallbacks).

## Revised stack at a glance
| Layer | R1 (Python) | R2 (Java) |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Python 3.12 + FastAPI | Java 17 target / Boot 4.1.2 / Temurin 21 |
| Parse+validate | PyYAML + own checks | Swagger Parser 2.1.48 + own collect-all walk |
| YAML | PyYAML | Jackson 3 YAML |
| DB | SQLite | H2 file mode (+ in-memory tests) |
| DAO | raw sqlite3 | `JdbcTemplate` + `schema.sql` |
| Tests | pytest | JUnit 5 + `@SpringBootTest`/MockMvc/TestRestTemplate |
| Notify | urllib | Spring `RestClient` |
| Compose | override file | same override file, multi-stage Java Dockerfile |

## Implementation sequence (revised hour plan)
Same milestones and the **1:45–2:00 E2E demo checkpoint**, with a Java-specific hour 0: JAVA_HOME fix → `pom.xml` → **`dependency:go-offline` warm-up started in the background** → skeleton + `schema.sql` + health endpoint → compose override. Package structure mirrors the Python module plan 1:1 (`specs`, `compatibility`, `consumers`, `impact`, `policy`, `domain`, `audit`, `notify`, `api`, `persistence`).

## New risks / trade-offs flagged (DECISIONS A-15..A-17, B-08..B-10)
1. **Stale JAVA_HOME → JDK 8** — pre-empted by a mandatory hour-0 fix; Docker build path is env-independent as fallback (A-15).
2. **Boot 4 ↔ Swagger Parser Jackson split** (Jackson 3 vs Jackson 2) — coexist by design; containment rule B-10 keeps our own serialization on Jackson 3.
3. **Boot 3.5/4.0 support cliffs** — avoided by targeting 4.1; 4.2 explicitly not chased (GA only 2026-11-30).
4. First Maven/Docker builds download a lot — background warm-up + slim-jar Dockerfile fallback (A-17).
5. H2 single-process file lock; UTF-8 encoding pinned (local default is Cp1252).

Everything product-level — the 5-rule policy, ~15 compatibility rule codes, impact tiers, state machine, 9-table schema, API surface, and every test scenario from the recon — is preserved verbatim. Ready for your review before implementation starts.

-- Contract Guard registry schema (H2). CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so restarts are safe.
-- Design: PLAN.md §4. spec_versions rows exist only for versions that became current;
-- rejected/blocked attempts live in publication_attempts + audit.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS services (
    id          IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    slug        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    title       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    owner_team  VARCHAR(255),
    created_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spec_versions (
    id               IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    service_id       BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES services(id),
    version          VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    source_sha       VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    source_filename  VARCHAR(255),
    raw_yaml         CLOB NOT NULL,
    canonical_json   CLOB NOT NULL,
    effective_json   CLOB NOT NULL,
    state            VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('published', 'superseded')),
    published_at     TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    CONSTRAINT uq_spec_version UNIQUE (service_id, version)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS publication_attempts (
    id                IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    service_id        BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES services(id),
    incoming_version  VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    source_sha        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    raw_yaml          CLOB NOT NULL,
    canonical_json    CLOB,
    state             VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (state IN (
                        'received', 'rejected', 'auto_published', 'pending_ack',
                        'blocked', 'published', 'overridden_published',
                        'abandoned', 'failed')),
    breaking_count    INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    required_action   VARCHAR(64),
    created_at        TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    decided_at        TIMESTAMP,
    decided_by        VARCHAR(255),
    justification     CLOB,
    note              CLOB
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS findings (
    id          IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    attempt_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES publication_attempts(id),
    code        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    severity    VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('breaking', 'warn', 'info')),
    scope       VARCHAR(64),
    method      VARCHAR(16),
    path        VARCHAR(512),
    location    VARCHAR(255),
    field_path  VARCHAR(512),
    detail      CLOB,
    old_json    CLOB,
    new_json    CLOB
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finding_impacts (
    id             IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    finding_id     BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES findings(id),
    consumer       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    level          VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (level IN ('affected', 'possible', 'none')),
    evidence_json  CLOB
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS consumer_definitions (
    id          IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    team        VARCHAR(255),
    raw_yaml    CLOB NOT NULL,
    source_sha  VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    active      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    replaced_at TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS consumer_bindings (
    id           IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    consumer_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES consumer_definitions(id),
    provider_slug VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    method       VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
    path_raw     VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    path_shape   VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    sends_json   CLOB NOT NULL,
    reads_json   CLOB NOT NULL
);

-- Append-only audit trail; rows are never updated or deleted.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attempt_transitions (
    id          IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    attempt_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES publication_attempts(id),
    from_state  VARCHAR(32),
    to_state    VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    actor       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    comment     CLOB,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notifications (
    id            IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    kind          VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    service       VARCHAR(255),
    version       VARCHAR(64),
    payload_json  CLOB NOT NULL,
    target_url    VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    status        VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    created_at    TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    delivered_at  TIMESTAMP
);

/**
 * Compatibility engine: independent schema-level diff between two effective schema maps,
 * classified into stable rule codes with severity (breaking/warn/info), per the
 * guarantee-asymmetry principle in PLAN.md §6. Cosmetic reorganization must produce no
 * breaking findings.

Then implement the compatibility module. Design:

**Data model**: `CompatibilityFinding` record: code, severity (enum breaking/warn/info), scope (REQ/PARAM/RESP/OPERATION/PATH/REQUEST_BODY), method, path, pathShape, location (effective location key or field path), fieldPath, detail, oldJson, newJson.

**Diff engine input**: two `Map<String, String>` effective-schema maps (from SpecDocument.getEffectiveSchemas()), keyed by `EffectiveLocation.key()` = `VERB /pathShape :: scope`. Values are canonical JSON strings of the expanded schema (or "null" for schema-less).

**Structure of location keys**: `VERB /shape :: scope` where scope is `requestBody:<mt>`, `param:<in>:<n>`, `response:<status>[:<mt>]`.

Parsing: split on first " :: " → location part `VERB /shape`, scope part. 

**Diff algorithm**:
1. Compute set of location keys in old and new.
2. Operations: group keys by (verb, shape). An operation present in old but not new → OPERATION.REMOVED (breaking). Present in new but not old → OPERATION.ADDED (info).

```java
public final class CompatibilityEngine {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String, String> oldEffective, Map<String, String> newEffective) {

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String, String> oldEffective, Map<String, String> newEffective,
                                           Map<String, String> oldPathAliases, Map<String, String> newPathAliases) {
        List<CompatibilityFinding> findings = new ArrayList<>();
        Map<OpKey, Map<String, String>> oldOps = groupByOperation(oldEffective);
        Map<OpKey, Map<String, String>> newOps = groupByOperation(newEffective);
        for (OpKey op : union sorted) {
            Map<String,String> o = oldOps.getOrDefault(op, Map.of());
            Map<String,String> n = newOps.getOrDefault(op, Map.of());
            String method = op.verb(); String path = resolvePath(op.shape(), oldPathAliases, newPathAliases);
            if (!oldOps.containsKey(op)) { findings.add(OPERATION.ADDED info); continue; }
            if (!newOps.containsKey(op)) { findings.add(OPERATION.REMOVED breaking, detail scopes); continue; }
            diffOperation(method, path, op.shape(), o, n, findings);
        }
        sort findings;
        return findings;
    }
```

```java
    static Op opOf(String key) {
        int sep = key.indexOf(" :: ");
        String left = sep >= 0 ? key.substring(0, sep) : key;
        int sp = left.indexOf(' ');
        if (sp <= 0) return new Op("", left);
        return new Op(left.substring(0, sp), left.substring(sp + 1));
```

```java
package com.contractguard.compatibility;

import ...;

public final class CompatibilityEngine {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    private static final List<String> CONSTRAINT_KEYS = List.of(
        "minimum", "maximum", "minLength", "maxLength", "minItems", "maxItems",
        "pattern", "multipleOf", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum", "uniqueItems");

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String,String> oldE, Map<String,String> newE) {
        return diff(oldE, newE, Map.of(), Map.of());
    }

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String,String> oldE, Map<String,String> newE,
                                           Map<String,String> oldAliases, Map<String,String> newAliases) {
        List<CompatibilityFinding> out = new ArrayList<>();
        Map<Op, Map<String,String>> oldOps = group(oldE);
        Map<Op, Map<String,String>> newOps = group(newE);
        TreeSet<Op> ops = new TreeSet<>();
        ops.addAll(oldOps.keySet()); ops.addAll(newOps.keySet());
        for (Op op : ops) {
            String method = op.verb();
            String path = op.shape();
            Map<String,String> o = oldOps.get(op), n = newOps.get(op);
            if (o == null) {
                out.add(new CompatibilityFinding("OPERATION.ADDED", Severity.INFO, "OPERATION",
                        method, path, null, null, "new operation", null, null));
                continue;
            }
            if (n == null) {
                out.add(new CompatibilityFinding("OPERATION.REMOVED", Severity.BREAKING, "OPERATION",
                        method, path, null, null,
                        "operation removed; dropped wire locations: " + String.join(", ", sortedKeys(o)),
                        null, null));
                continue;
            }
            String resolvedPath = newAliases.getOrDefault(op.shape(), oldAliases.getOrDefault(op.shape(), op.shape()));
            diffOperation(method, resolvedPath, op.shape(), o, n, out);
        }
        out.sort(Comparator.comparing(CompatibilityFinding::location, Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder()))
                .thenComparing(CompatibilityFinding::fieldPath, Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder()))
                .thenComparing(CompatibilityFinding::code));
        return out;
    }
```

```java
package com.contractguard.compatibility;

public final class CompatibilityEngine {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String, String> oldEffective, Map<String, String> newEffective) {
        return diff(oldEffective, newEffective, Map.of(), Map.of());
    }

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String, String> oldEffective, Map<String, String> newEffective,
                                           Map<String, String> oldPathAliases, Map<String, String> newPathAliases) {
        List<CompatibilityFinding> findings = new ArrayList<>();
        Map<OpKey, Map<String, String>> oldOps = groupByOperation(oldEffective);
        Map<OpKey, Map<String, String>> newOps = groupByOperation(newEffective);
        for (OpKey op : union sorted) {
            Map<String,String> o = oldOps.getOrDefault(op, Map.of());
            Map<String,String> n = newOps.getOrDefault(op, Map.of());
            String method = op.verb(); String path = resolvePath(op.shape(), oldPathAliases, newPathAliases);
            if (!oldOps.containsKey(op)) { findings.add(OPERATION.ADDED info); continue; }
            if (!newOps.containsKey(op)) { findings.add(OPERATION.REMOVED breaking, detail scopes); continue; }
            diffOperation(method, path, op.shape(), o, n, findings);
        }
        sort findings;
        return findings;
    }
```

```java
final class LocationKeys {
    record Op(String verb, String shape) implements Comparable<Op> {...}
    static Op opOf(String key) {
        int sep = key.indexOf(" :: ");
        String left = sep >= 0 ? key.substring(0, sep) : key;
        int sp = left.indexOf(' ');
        if (sp <= 0) return new Op("", left);
        return new Op(left.substring(0, sp), left.substring(sp + 1));
    }
    static String scopeOf(String key) {
        int sep = key.indexOf(" :: ");
        return sep >= 0 ? key.substring(sep + 4) : "";
    }
}
```

```java
package com.contractguard.compatibility;

import ...;

public final class CompatibilityEngine {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    private static final List<String> CONSTRAINT_KEYS = List.of(
        "minimum", "maximum", "minLength", "maxLength", "minItems", "maxItems",
        "pattern", "multipleOf", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum", "uniqueItems");

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String,String> oldE, Map<String,String> newE) {
        return diff(oldE, newE, Map.of(), Map.of());
    }

    public List<CompatibilityFinding> diff(Map<String,String> oldE, Map<String,String> newE,
                                           Map<String,String> oldAliases, Map<String,String> newAliases) {
        List<CompatibilityFinding> out = new ArrayList<>();
        Map<Op, Map<String,String>> oldOps = group(oldE);
        Map<Op, Map<String,String>> newOps = group(newE);
        TreeSet<Op> ops = new TreeSet<>();
        ops.addAll(oldOps.keySet()); ops.addAll(newOps.keySet());
        for (Op op : ops) {
            String method = op.verb();
            String path = op.shape();
            Map<String,String> o = oldOps.get(op), n = newOps.get(op);
            if (o == null) {
                out.add(new CompatibilityFinding("OPERATION.ADDED", Severity.INFO, "OPERATION",
                        method, path, null, null, "new operation", null, null));
                continue;
            }
            if (n == null) {
                out.add(new CompatibilityFinding("OPERATION.REMOVED", Severity.BREAKING, "OPERATION",
                        method, path, null, null,
                        "operation removed; dropped wire locations: " + String.join(", ", sortedKeys(o)),
                        null, null));
                continue;
            }
            String resolvedPath = newAliases.getOrDefault(op.shape(), oldAliases.getOrDefault(op.shape(), op.shape()));
            diffOperation(method, resolvedPath, op.shape(), o, n, out);
        }
        out.sort(Comparator.comparing(CompatibilityFinding::location, Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder()))
                .thenComparing(CompatibilityFinding::fieldPath, Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder()))
                .thenComparing(CompatibilityFinding::code));
        return out;
    }
```

```java
private static Set<String> typeSet(JsonNode schema) {
    JsonNode t = schema.get("type");
    if (t == null || t.isNull() || t.isMissingNode()) return Set.of();
    if (t.isString()) return Set.of(t.stringValue());
    Set<String> out = new TreeSet<>();
    for (JsonNode e : t) out.add(e.isString() ? e.stringValue() : e.asText());
    return out;
}
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Contract Guard (API contract registry + breaking-change detection) in Java/Spring Boot per revised PLAN.md/DECISIONS.md. Currently in Phase 1 (scaffold) + Phase 2 (`specs` module with Swagger Parser, validation, $ref resolution, effective schemas). Must stop after scaffold + specs module are implemented and tested, then report results.

## Requirements
- Never modify `specs/`, `consumers/`, `webhook-receiver/`, or original `docker-compose.yml` (read-only evaluation fixtures).
- No hardcoded fixture-filename-based expectations in tests; do not skip failing tests.
- Keep compatibility detection, consumer impact, publishing policy, persistence as separate modules.
- No fake/placeholder business logic.
- Use: Java 17 release, Spring Boot 4.1.2, Spring Web MVC, Spring JDBC, Bean Validation, H2, Swagger Parser 2.1.48, Jackson YAML 3 (tools.jackson), JUnit 5 + Spring Boot Test.
- Maven requires `$env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.0.13.9-hotspot"` before every invocation (default JAVA_HOME points at JDK 1.8; `mvn -v` must report Java 21).
- Publish policy (5 rules): non-breaking=auto-publish; breaking no-impact=warn+ack; breaking with affected consumers=block+override with mandatory justification; invalid spec=reject unconditionally; semver never trusted alone.
- Five-hour hackathon budget; E2E demo checkpoint within first 2 hours.

## Decisions
- Stack: Spring Boot 4.1.2 parent POM, Java 17 target, Temurin 21 toolchain, H2 file mode + JdbcTemplate (no ORM/JPA), swagger-parser 2.1.48, Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) for own YAML/JSON, Mockito-free pure JUnit for core, static vanilla JS frontend, RestClient for webhooks to untouched Python receiver on port 9900 (path `/contractguard`).
- Path shape normalization: `/quotes/{id}` ≡ `/quotes/{quoteId}` → `/quotes/{0}`.
- Duplicate version: identical re-upload = idempotent 200; differing content = 409; version regression = 409.
- `x-internal` is a badge not exemption; `x-sunset` is enforceable deadline; override authority = justification + `X-Acting-User` header.
- Impact tiers: AFFECTED gates, POSSIBLE warns, NONE clears.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reconnaissance of all 12 spec files, 4 consumer files, webhook receiver (documented in PLAN.md/DECISIONS.md).
- Fixture integrity verified (all 20 kit files SHA-256 hashed, sizes unchanged).
- JAVA_HOME fix verified (`mvn -v` reports Java 21.0.13).
- `pom.xml` created (Boot 4.1.2, swagger-parser 2.1.48, jackson-dataformat-yaml, H2, starters web/jdbc/validation/test).
- Dependency warm-up `mvn -B -q dependency:go-offline` completed successfully (local repo populated).

Both commits are in. Final report:

## Milestone Report

### Git
```
b9ba8a4 feat: implement API compatibility and semver analysis   (15 files, +1784/−8)
5944b84 feat: scaffold Spring Boot application and OpenAPI validation  (61 files)
```
Pre-commit verification: all 19 kit fixtures **byte-identical to baseline** (SHA-256, re-checked after the test runs); staged set contains no build output, database files, or temp artifacts.

### What was built

**`compatibility` module** — `CompatibilityEngine` diffs the **effective wire-contract maps** from the specs module (key = `VERB /pathShape :: scope`, value = canonical `$ref`-free schema JSON). It never touches YAML: it consumes the parser's output and only re-reads the canonical JSON strings. Helpers: `CompatibilityFinding`, `Severity`, `SchemaSide`, `LocationKeys`.

Semantics implemented, in your priority order:
- **Request/response asymmetry**: requests may only *accept more* (narrowing breaks); responses may only *promise more* (weakened guarantees break). Same physical change → opposite severities per side.
- **Required add/remove**: `REQ.REQUIRED_ADDED` breaking / `RESP.REQUIRED_ADDED` info (guarantee strengthened), mirrored for removals.
- **Enums**: `*_ENUM_NARROWED` / `*_ENUM_WIDENED` with asymmetric severity.
- **Types & constraints**: `TYPE_NARROWED/WIDENED/CHANGED` plus directional `CONSTRAINT_TIGHTENED`/`CONSTRAINT_LOOSENED` (tightening breaks request senders; loosening breaks strict response readers; `nullable`, min/max, pattern, uniqueItems handled).
- **Rename detection**: a removed+added property pair with deep-equal canonical shape collapses to one `PROPERTY_RENAMED`; different shapes stay REMOVED+ADDED. **Rename↔required interplay fixed**: the old required list is re-keyed through detected renames, so renaming required `amount`→`value` is one finding, not four.
- **Operations/response codes/media types**: removed → breaking, added → info; schema-less responses gaining/losing bodies handled.
- **Required `region` param**: parameter envelopes now carry their `required` flag (small specs-module extension), matched by `(in, ordinal)` with names stripped — so path-param renames stay invisible (cosmetic) while a new required param is `PARAM.REQUIRED_ADDED`.

**`policy` module** — deliberately separate channel: `Semver` (parse/bump), `VersionPolicyAnalyzer` emitting `VERSION.POLICY.BREAKING_WITHOUT_MAJOR` (warn), `MAJOR_WITHOUT_BREAKING` (info), `UNPARSEABLE` skip. Policy findings decorate only — they never gate.

### Test results
**Tests run: 58, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 — BUILD SUCCESS** (28 specs + 21 compatibility + 9 policy).

Kit-pair outcomes (real specs, effective-schema based):
- **quote 1.0.0→1.1.0**: **zero findings** (renamed components, inlined models, renamed path param — no false positives)
- **quote 1.1.0→2.0.0**: 5 breaking — 2× `RESP.PROPERTY_RENAMED` (`premium.breakdown[].amount`→`value`, POST+GET), 2× `RESP.ENUM_WIDENED` (`status` + `EXPIRED`), 1× `PARAM.REQUIRED_ADDED` (`region`, `param:query:1` on the internal cache purge)
- **policy 2.0.0→3.0.0**: 4× `RESP.PROPERTY_REMOVED` (`legacyCode`, `holder.phone` on both the list and item responses; array items get `[]`-prefixed paths)
- **policy 3.0.0→4.0.0**: 2 breaking — `REQ.REQUIRED_ADDED` (`requestedBy`), `REQ.ENUM_NARROWED` (`VEHICLE` dropped) — the stealth-change pair
- **claims 3.0.0→4.0.0**: 2× `RESP.REQUIRED_REMOVED` (`amountApproved` no longer guaranteed) + new 202 response (info); **claims 1→3** and **quote 2→3**: purely additive, nothing breaking

Failures fixed along the way: 1 real engine gap (constraint direction codes), 1 engine-correctness fix (rename/required re-keying, discovered from the actual kit data), 3 wrong test expectations, 3 broken synthetic-YAML constructions, and a systematic misuse of `noneSatisfy` with boolean lambdas (no-op consumers "satisfy" vacuously).

### Not started (per instruction)
Consumer impact, publishing policy/gate, persistence, pipeline splice, webhooks/audit.

**Next concrete step**: the `consumers` module — parse the 4 consumer YAML files into declared usage (operations + response field paths), map against findings to produce AFFECTED/POSSIBLE/NONE tiers, then splice into the pipeline for the E2E demo checkpoint.
